title: Backend senior systemdesign search indexing backend
topic: Backend senior systemdesign search indexing backend
question: Design the backend for large-scale search over a catalog of hundreds of millions of documents (e.g. product listings) that get created, updated, and deleted continuously, with search results expected to reflect recent changes within a few seconds.
idealAnswer:
Separates the write path (ingesting document changes) from the read path (serving search queries), and explains why the primary database isn't suited for full-text/faceted search at this scale, motivating a dedicated inverted-index-based search store

Describes keeping the search index in sync with the source of truth via an async pipeline, e.g. a change stream or event log (like CDC or a message queue) feeding indexing workers, rather than writing to the search index synchronously in the same request as the source-of-truth write

Addresses horizontal scaling of the index itself, sharding the index across multiple nodes since it won't fit or perform well on one machine, and fanning a query out to relevant shards and merging results

Explains the near-real-time freshness requirement concretely, e.g. index refresh intervals, and acknowledges the tradeoff between indexing throughput and how quickly a write becomes visible in search results

Considers relevance and ranking as a real design concern, not just retrieval, e.g. combining text match scores with business signals (popularity, recency), and mentions the need to reindex or backfill when ranking logic changes
